target_customer: Urban consumers in Nigeria (later Ghana) ordering meals, plus restaurants and stores that pay commission to be listed and delivered
problem: Food delivery in Lagos was slow and unreliable, with delivery times often above 30 minutes and heavy discount dependence among rivals.
business_model: marketplace take rate plus delivery fees, later ads and subscription (Chowpass)
product_category: on-demand food and grocery delivery marketplace

founders.name: Femi Aluko
founders.background_notes: YC page: Principal Engineer at Paystack, joined in 2017 as fifth engineer. Education not stated on YC page.

founders.name: Olumide Ojo
founders.background_notes: YC page: about five years at African fintechs including Paystack as Principal Engineer.

founders.name: Lanre Yusuf
founders.background_notes: YC page: Engineering Lead at Crown Interactive.

competitors.name: Jumia Food
competitors.what: Food delivery marketplace across Africa including Nigeria
competitors.traction_then: Operating in Nigeria; later ceased operations in December 2023

competitors.name: Glovo
competitors.what: On-demand delivery app operating in Nigeria
competitors.traction_then: Active in Lagos market per later coverage

competitors.name: Bolt Food
competitors.what: Food delivery from ride-hailing company Bolt
competitors.traction_then: Active in Nigeria per later coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: A three-sided marketplace with dispatch and rider logistics, built by engineers from Paystack; standard engineering, hard parts are operations.

defensibility.rationale: Delivery apps are copyable; edge came from faster delivery under 30 minutes and restricted discounting, which is operational rather than structural.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Jumia Food exited in December 2023 and some foreign players scaled back in Nigeria and Ghana per 2025 coverage, leaving market share to local operators.

market_need_then: Lagos had demand for food delivery but rivals averaged more than 30 minute deliveries and relied on discounts, per Chowdeck coverage; the YC listing cites 80,000 meals delivered in six months.

branding.domain_note: Uses chowdeck.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark; a C CHOWDECK trademark application was filed in the US on 2025-09-17
identity.visual_style: Clean and friendly website with step by step guidance
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, casual, greets in English, Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa; tagline Deliver happiness

branding.brand_signature: Localized multilingual greeting and the line Deliver happiness

brand_strength.rationale: Strong local recognition implied by 1.5 million customers, but no source on the brand itself; rating reflects limited evidence.

outcome_analysis: Chowdeck grew from a Lagos food delivery startup into a multi-country platform. It reached 1 billion naira monthly order value by November 2023, raised a 2.5 million seed in April 2024 and a 9 million Series A in August 2025, while rivals such as Jumia Food exited. It cut 68 percent of contract staff in 2024 citing process gains and acquired Mira in 2025.
notes: Competitor sources are dated 2023-11, about 17 months after the batch; Glovo and Bolt Food presence in 2022 not independently dated. Seed investor lists differ across outlets. Guardian Nigeria headline describes Series A as from 8 foreign investors; other outlets name Novastar as lead. Education of founders not found.
